items.q: On a 1920 by 1080 screen, which pixel is at the lower-right corner?
rationales: Coordinates start at 0, so the last column is 1919 and the last row 1079; onScreen(1920, 1080) is False.
x is the horizontal coordinate, so the width comes first.

items.q: The pointer is at (100, 200). Which call leaves it at (100, 500)?
rationales: move() is relative, so this ends at (100, 700).
moveTo(500) sets only x, so this ends at (500, 200); None is what keeps a coordinate.

items.q: hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 'shift', 's') sends its key-up events in which order?
options: all four at the same moment
rationales: That is the order of the key-down events; the releases come in the reverse order.
Each key-up is a separate event, sent one after the other.

items.q: How many drag calls does the chapter's spiralDraw.py make, starting from distance = 300 with change = 20?
rationales: 16 is twice the number of passes of the loop, and each pass makes four drag calls.
30 is the number of button presses: two of the 32 calls drag by (0, 0), and a drag of zero sends nothing.

items.q: What text does write(['a', 'b', 'left', 'left', 'X', 'Y']) leave in an empty text field?
rationales: That would be the result without the two left arrows.
That would be the result with only one left arrow.

items.q: Which statement about press('notakey') is correct for PyAutoGUI 0.9.54?
options: It does nothing and raises nothing; isValidKey('notakey') is False
It types the letters n, o, t, a, k, e and y
rationales: No exception is raised for an unknown key name.
press() takes one key name, not a string of characters to type; write() types characters.

items.q: The pointer has just reached the upper-left corner through moveTo(0, 0) with the fail-safe on. When is FailSafeException raised?
options: Only after PAUSE seconds have passed
rationales: A move that ends on a fail-safe point is itself exempt from the check.
PAUSE only delays the end of a call; the check runs at the start of the next one.

items.q: With the default pause, about how long do ten PyAutoGUI calls wait in total?
rationales: 0.1 second is the pause after one call.
10 seconds would need a pause of 1 second after each call.

items.q: A screen pixel is (255, 255, 254). What does pixelMatchesColor(x, y, (255, 255, 255)) return with the default tolerance?
rationales: The default tolerance is 0, so the match is exact; tolerance=1 would give True.
That exception belongs to the locate functions, not to pixelMatchesColor.

items.q: A picture given to locateOnScreen() is not on the screen. What happens in PyAutoGUI 0.9.54?
options: It returns a Box of zeros
rationales: None is returned only after useImageNotFoundException(False) has been called.
No Box is returned when there is no match.

items.q: The chapter prints pyautogui.pixel((50, 200)). Why does that line fail in PyAutoGUI 0.9.54?
options: pixel needs the two coordinates as separate arguments, pixel(x, y)
pixel was removed from the library
rationales: pixel() is defined for the platforms PyScreeze supports; the tuple form is what fails.
pixel() is still there; it takes x and y as two arguments.

items.q: What happens when a Linux script calls pyautogui.getActiveWindow?
options: It raises AttributeError, because the name is only defined on Windows
rationales: The window functions are implemented only for Windows.
An empty list is what the search functions return on Windows when nothing matches.
